brief.whyItMatters: Your client work is building with models, so a change in how agents, tools or evals behave changes what you can ship and how you test it.

keyConcepts.explanation: A program in which a model picks a tool, reads the result and decides the next step, repeating until the task is done or a limit stops it.
The model returns a structured request to call a function you defined. Your code runs it and sends the result back as the next message.

brief.whyItMatters: The platform is the one dependency every web project shares. A feature reaching all browsers removes a library, and a regression explains a bug you did not write.

keyConcepts.explanation: A label from the web standards community that tells you a feature works in all major browsers, and since when.
A browser API that animates between two DOM states or two pages by snapshotting old and new, with no animation library.

brief.whatHappened: "OpenCode Hacked: User credentials leaked" reached the Hacker News front page with 864 points and 161 comments.
brief.whyItMatters: A flaw found in someone else's stack is often present in yours. Reading the attack tells you which assumption to check in your own code.

keyConcepts.explanation: A public identifier for one specific vulnerability, so advisories, scanners and patches can refer to the same flaw.
A list of what you protect, who might attack it and where trust changes hands. It tells you which defences are worth building.
